children: Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast were mostly steady on Tuesday as traders waited to see whether a US-China summit this week would boost Chinese demand for American farm goods.

Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures weakened after rallying on Monday on hopes for US agriculture deals with China ahead of Thursday's planned meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Traders want to see whether China, the world's biggest soybean importer, agrees to purchases and the removal of a 10% import duty on US soybeans.
Chinese state-owned buyers have bought US soybeans. However, traders hope private Chinese buyers could resume purchases if Beijing removes the 10% import duty.

CIF soybean barges loaded in September were bid steady at 78 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, while barges loaded in October were also unchanged, bid at 90 cents over November futures.
Corn barges loaded in November were bid at 91 cents over December futures. Barges loaded in January, February and March were bid at 88 cents over March futures, all steady.
